text:
sarah: Heads-up — getting a customer escalations email about large p99 spikes after last night's runtime rollout. They see many 429s to our auth proxy and end-to-end tail latency up ~3x. link: https://support.example.com/INC-1298 :eyes:
ops-bot: deploy v2026.03.16-runtime-kernelex landed to canary at 2026-03-16T02:12Z on 10% traffic (canary-group A)
devon: seeing same in staging canary traces. p95 stable, p99 jumps around 800-1200ms for text-gen paths that touch billing/auth lookup. stack shows lots of waits in auth_client.request()
mike: confirming logs show auth proxy returning 429s with header `X-RateLimit-Reset` set but our client retries are immediate (no backoff). suspect token refresh/renew loop introduced in runtime auth middleware change.
julia: which PR changed auth middleware? I can bisect.
sarah: PR #9245 — changed token refresh logic to eagerly refresh if ttl < 5m instead of <30s. The idea was to reduce latency on new requests, but maybe it causes stampeding refreshes under concurrency.
devon: repro steps I ran in staging (small k8s):
```
# replay workload hitting canary
hey replay --qps 50 --concurrency 20 --target https://canary.runtime.internal/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer redwood-test' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-1","prompt":"hello"}'
```
results: 5% 429s from auth proxy, p99 ~950ms, auth_client logs show repeated `refresh_token` calls per request.
mike: sample log snippet from canary pod `runtime-abc-2`:
```
2026-03-16T02:34:11.123Z auth_client INFO refresh_token start tenant=acct-123
2026-03-16T02:34:11.124Z auth_proxy WARN rate_limit tenant=acct-123 limit=200 window=60s
2026-03-16T02:34:11.125Z auth_client INFO refresh_token success tenant=acct-123 latency_ms=57
2026-03-16T02:34:11.126Z auth_client INFO refresh_token start tenant=acct-123
2026-03-16T02:34:11.127Z auth_client ERROR refresh_token throttled tenant=acct-123 status=429
```
sarah: ok hypothesis: eager refresh change caused many concurrent workers to hit auth service and exhaust tenant-rated limits. That cascades back to runtime as 429 + retries => queuing, raising p99.
julia: plan: 1) scale canary auth client pool to 1 (single serial refresh) as experiment; 2) revert PR or change to randomized jitter + exponential backoff on 429s; 3) roll traffic to previous runtime for affected customers.
devon: temporary mitigation: add middleware to short-circuit refresh under heavy refresh failures: if refresh_throttle_count > 5 in 60s for tenant -> treat current token as valid for +30s and add small randomized jitter to future refresh attempts.
mike: can run a hotfix to canary via patch release (no full rollback) to implement short-circuit. I can build and push within 30m.
sarah: support -> proactively notify affected customers and set expectation; set incident priority P2 until rollback/hotfix. @julia please start bisect: between runtime kernel change and auth-middleware change, which one introduced the behavior?
julia: starting bisect now. hypothesis: auth change is the main suspect but kernel batching change could increase concurrency per worker and exacerbate. I'll flip auth middleware back to previous TTL threshold on 2 canary pods and run replay.
devon: results after flipping auth TTL on two pods: 0.5% 429s, p99 down to ~420ms for those pods. other pods remain high.
julia: that's a pretty strong signal pointing at PR #9245. moving to rollback auth change in canary A and schedule full rollback in next 15m if metrics improve.
ops-bot: canary-group A traffic split updated: 10% -> 5% to v2026.03.16-runtime-kernelex, 5% -> v2026.03.15-stable (rolled back for auth-middle).
mike: metrics after partial rollback: canary p99 aggregate dropped from 980ms -> 510ms in 10 minutes. 429 rate cut by 70%.
sarah: good. action items:
- mike: hotfix to add short-circuit + jitter backport to v2026.03.16 (ETA 30m)
- julia: open PR to revert eager-refresh behavior and add proper leader election for refresh per-tenant (ETA 2 days)
- devon: run full bisect across kernel batching changes to confirm no other regressions (ETA 1 day)
- support: notify affected customers and provide timeline + rollback notice (sarah will handle)
- ops: monitor auth proxy per-tenant rate usage dashboards and add alert if >70% of quota used in 1m window.

mike: adding quick mitigation patch: if refresh returns 429 -> backoff 200-600ms with randomized jitter and mark tenant as 'throttled' for 1s. I'll push canary hotfix now.
julia: will follow up with a test that simulates token refresh stampede and assert we don't exceed N concurrent refreshes per tenant.
sarah: thanks team. keeping this thread pinned to the incident. once hotfix is stable we'll close. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident INC-1298 assigned -> owner=sarah, severity=P2, created=2026-03-16T03:05Z
